title: Riverstone - Dedicated capacity discovery
summary: Discovery call to evaluate Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive, regulated inference workloads. Discussed reserved GPU sizing, burst strategy, networking/VPC isolation, compliance (SOC 2/KMS), and next steps for a pilot/benchmark.
next_steps: Redwood to send dedicated capacity pricing and SKU options (Jamie)
Redwood to share SOC2 + security pack and network setup guide (Sanjay)
Customer to share sample traffic profile and 7-day p99 latency targets (Laura)
Schedule technical bench run for week of Nov 9 (all)
Follow-up call to finalize pilot scope in 1 week
action_items: Jamie Park: Send pricing SKUs and sample contract by 2026-11-02
Sanjay Patel: Share SOC2 report, security pack, and VPC peering guide by 2026-10-30
Laura Chen: Provide anonymized traffic profile and target latencies by 2026-11-03
Tom Reyes: Confirm internal procurement timeline by 2026-11-05
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh I'm Jamie from Redwood, AE on the account. Sanjay from our solutions engineering team is here too. quick intro?
[00:08] Laura Chen: Hi all, Laura Chen head of ML at Riverstone, Tom CTO, Aisha infra lead, Miguel product. thanks for making time.
[00:15] Jamie Park: Great thanks. The goal today is to understand your workload, requirements for dedicated capacity and whether Hosted or Dedicated or Private makes sense, and next steps for a pilot.
[00:24] Tom Reyes: high level, we run document processing and customer-chat assistants. latency is big for us, want predictable p99 under 150ms on text gen path and data isolation is required since we process PII in some flows.
[00:36] Sanjay Patel: ok good, can you share current traffic patterns and model sizes?
[00:40] Laura Chen: sure, most requests are single-turn, average seq len ~256 tokens, bursty during business hours, peak 1800 rps for embeddings, generation peaks are lower ~400 rps. models are a mix of 13B and 70B open models, we are evaluating quantized variants.
[01:00] Aisha Khan: infra constraints: we prefer reserved GPUs for cost predictability, and we need VPC isolation - can't send traffic over public endpoints for some flows.
[01:07] Jamie Park: understood. so Dedicated sounds like the primary option, possibly Private if you need full control of the control plane. can I ask about your tolerance for fallbacks? if a dedicated pool is saturated do you want automatic fallback to hosted capacity?
[01:19] Miguel Ortiz: we'd like a configurable policy. ideally we can burst to shared infra for non-PII traffic but keep PII on reserved nodes.
[01:27] Sanjay Patel: that's a common pattern. Redwood supports routing policies by tag, so you can route PII to dedicated pools and allow non-sensitive traffic to overflow to hosted. the routing supports model variants too - cheaper quantized variants on overflow.
[01:43] Tom Reyes: cool. on bursts, how fast does autoscaling react? we worry about startup latency for additional instances, especially for 70B models.
[01:51] Sanjay Patel: good question. for Dedicated we recommend a steady base of reserved GPUs sized for typical peak, plus burst pool or reserved burst capacity. our autoscaler can add nodes, but cold start for large weights can be tens of seconds to a couple minutes depending on GPU and model format. we mitigate with warm-standby processes and continuous prewarmed kernels when configured.
[02:12] Laura Chen: okay so we should right-size reserved capacity for p99 spikes and rely on burst for tail events. what about performance variance across GPU types? we mainly use A100s internally.
[02:22] Jamie Park: Redwood's scheduler optimizes kernel selection per hardware. A100 or H100 both supported; H100 will give better throughput and lower latency for 70B models generally. we can provide benchmark profiles per model/hardware.
[02:34] Aisha Khan: We need network setup details. VPC peering vs private link? what's recommended?
[02:39] Sanjay Patel: we support VPC peering and PrivateLink; for strict egress controls customers use VPC peering + NAT/proxy in their VPC. our Private offering places the control plane in your VPC with optional on-prem packaging if needed.
[02:51] Tom Reyes: and what about keys and encryption? KMS + HSM?
[02:55] Jamie Park: we integrate with customer KMS and HSM, though sometimes the transcript from auto transcriber mixes that as K-M-S H-S-M, but yes we support customer-managed keys and in-flight TLS.
[03:07] Laura Chen: compliance: do you have SOC 2, ISO? we'll need audit logs and role-based access control.
[03:12] Sanjay Patel: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation, plus detailed audit logs, SSO/SAML, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC. I'll share the security pack after the call.
[03:23] Miguel Ortiz: pricing — reserved vs burst costs and commitment terms?
[03:25] Jamie Park: for Dedicated there's a reserved monthly commit pricing, smaller commit for burst. Typically two tiers: reserved nodes (monthly commit) and burst credits billed on use. I'll send SKU examples tailored to your throughput profile.
[03:38] Tom Reyes: how do you handle model updates and version pinning without disrupting traffic?
[03:43] Sanjay Patel: we support model version pinning and rolling canaries. you can define rollout percent and automatic rollback on quality regressions. the console has per-model dashboards so you can monitor latency and token-cost.
[03:53] Laura Chen: what about KV cache and prefix caching strategies? we've seen cost blow up without efficient caching.
[03:59] Sanjay Patel: Redwood has per-customer KV cache and prefix caching; we can persist caches to speed up warm requests. cache sharding is automatic. sometimes the auto transcript says K-V cash, but it's KV cache and it's critical for chat workloads.
[04:12] Aisha Khan: any limits on custom quantization/TF ops? we use some optimized kernels that are picky.
[04:18] Sanjay Patel: we have a model onboarding process. for custom kernels we typically test in our staging infra. quantized models are supported; on some hardware we recommend specific quant formats. we can run a compatibility check during the PoC.
[04:30] Jamie Park: earlier you mentioned data residency; are you required to keep data in certain regions?
[04:35] Laura Chen: yes, EU customer data must stay in eu-west-1. also logs for those interactions need to remain in the region.
[04:42] Sanjay Patel: we can route requests to region-specific pools and keep logs in region. our Dedicated offering can be provisioned in a selected cloud region.
[04:51] Tom Reyes: procurement timeline — we're aiming to decide before end of Q4, procurement signs off early December.
[04:57] Jamie Park: good to know. We'll align pilot timeline accordingly.
[05:01] Miguel Ortiz: for the pilot we want to run a perf benchmark with our 13B and 70B models at representative traffic. what's the typical benchmark cadence?
[05:10] Sanjay Patel: we usually do an initial perf run in our sandbox environment, then a dedicated bench on reserved hardware. the bench includes latency percentiles, throughput, and cost-per-token estimates. expect 2-3 days for full bench and data analysis.
[05:23] Laura Chen: do you provide tooling to replay traffic? we have some synthetic and real traces available.
[05:27] Sanjay Patel: yes we accept trace replays and synthetic loads. we'll need anonymized traces for any PII.
[05:33] Aisha Khan: security question — can we have IP allowlisting and private peering for admin APIs?
[05:38] Jamie Park: yes, admin access can be restricted via IP allowlist and SAML SSO; we also support tenant-level RBAC so only specific users can manage model rollouts.
[05:48] Tom Reyes: any gotchas around model cold-start for 70B when scaling out?
[05:52] Sanjay Patel: cold start can be mitigated with warm-standby and prewarming; for 70B we recommend keeping at least one warm replica per availability zone in heavy usage scenarios.
[06:02] Laura Chen: if we do a hybrid — reserved for PII, hosted fallback for non-PII — what's the telemetry look like? can we see per-route cost and token counts?
[06:11] Jamie Park: yep per-route token-level cost and latency, plus per-token traceability in the console. That's part of Redwood Console's observability surface.
[06:20] Miguel Ortiz: ok next steps recap?
[06:22] Jamie Park: I'll send pricing SKUs and a sample contract. Sanjay will share the SOC2 and security pack plus network setup guide. Laura to share traffic profile. We'll schedule the bench for week of Nov 9.
[06:33] Laura Chen: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:35] Tom Reyes: thanks, appreciate it.
[06:38] Jamie Park: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links to docs and next steps.
[06:45] (call ends)
questions: How fast does Dedicated autoscale for 70B models?
Can PII traffic be permanently isolated on reserved nodes?
What are the cold-start mitigations and recommended warm standby configurations?
